There's a function "holidays" that can generate holidays for a given country and year. The user specifically wants long weekends. That means holidays that fall on Friday or Monday (or maybe also if holiday falls on Saturday or Sunday but then extended). Usually long weekends are defined as holidays that create a 3-day weekend. For Canada, there are federal holidays. But the user might want all public holidays that create long weekends. We can compute which holidays in Canada in 2023 create a long weekend. We can use the "holidays" library to get all holidays for Canada in 2023. Then find those that fall on Friday or Monday. Also if holiday falls on Saturday or Sunday, we might consider the following Monday or preceding Friday as observed. But the question: "Could you fetch me the list of long weekends for Canada in the year 2023?" So we should produce a list of dates that are long weekends. We can interpret long weekend as any holiday that results in a 3-day weekend. That includes holidays that fall on Friday or Monday. Also if holiday falls on Saturday or Sunday, the observed day may be Monday or Friday. But the "holidays" library may provide observed dates. Let's check how the library works. The "holidays" library can generate holidays for Canada. It has an attribute "observed" that indicates whether the holiday is observed on a different day. But we can just use the library to get all holidays with observed days. Then we can filter those that are on Friday or Monday. But we also need to include holidays that are observed on Monday because the actual holiday falls on Sunday. But the library will mark the observed date as Monday. So we can just filter for holidays that are on Friday or Monday. That will give us the long weekend days. But we also need to output the holiday name. The user likely wants a list of long weekends. We can produce a table with date, holiday name, and maybe note if it's observed.

We can call the "holidays" function. The function signature: type holidays = (_: {country: string, years: number | number[], observed?: boolean, expand?: boolean, subdiv?: string | string[]}) => any; So we can call it with country="CA", years=2023, observed=true, expand=false. That will return a dictionary mapping dates to holiday names. Then we can iterate over the dictionary items, filter those where the date's weekday is Friday (weekday() == 4) or Monday (weekday() == 0). Then we can produce a list of those dates and holiday names.
